title: The overflow guard that disappears

cast.name: Nia
cast.role: Junior engineer convinced the check catches every overflow

cast.name: Len
cast.role: Calm reviewer who follows the arithmetic before trusting the branch

glossary.note: The language gives the program no required result for this operation.

glossary.full: Maximum value of the int type
glossary.note: A limit defined by the implementation's integer width.
Clang's runtime checks for selected undefined operations.

key_points: A signed-overflow test that performs the overflow first is already invalid.
For defined signed addition, n + 1 cannot be less than n.
Check bounds before arithmetic, and use sanitizers to expose executed bad paths.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Nia submits an overflow guard in code review. The function appears without its result.

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.text: If increment wraps, n plus one gets smaller. My condition catches that first. Which input breaks my reasoning?

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: Use the largest representable int. INT_MAX names that boundary. The guard calculates n plus one before comparing it with n.

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.text: I thought it wrapped around. Would the comparison become true?

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: For signed C integers, an unrepresentable result is undefined behavior, not guaranteed wraparound. The program has left the language’s promised behavior before comparison.

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.text: A compiler reasons about defined executions. There, adding one is greater than n, so the branch cannot be true.

out: Example inspection command; not run here.

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: That is the disappearing guard. Compile a small harness with UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer and pass the maximum int. It can catch signed overflow when that path executes.

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.text: Check the range before adding, or use checked arithmetic. A sanitizer reports executed paths; it cannot prove unseen inputs safe.

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: Never ask an overflowing expression to certify itself. Keep the range check first; sanitizer coverage is evidence, not a universal proof.
